goal: Start Kolibri Factory as a 24/7 distributed agent mesh: Control Plane must dispatch real work to server agents, agents must create follow-up/repair tasks for each other through Control Plane, and the owner must see live task ids, statuses, node capacity and blockers.
objective: On a server/control node, launch the first operational factory wave. Submit child tasks through Control Plane to fresh working nodes, require each node to report Agent Host/MIMO/GitHub/resource readiness, start safe non-production helper workers only when already installed and inactive, create repair tasks for nodes that are stale/degraded/unreachable, and produce exact artifacts listing child task ids, statuses, agents, server capacity, blockers and next dispatch wave. Do not perform destructive actions. Do not fake readiness.

child_task_template.goal: Report live node readiness for 24/7 factory work and create repair follow-ups for blockers.

required_node_checks: MIMO binary/process/auth readiness without printing secrets
GitHub clone/fetch/auth classification without printing credentials
disk, memory, CPU and queue pressure
safe capacity estimate for MIMO/subagents up to target 20
logical agent capacity contribution toward global target 1000
repair task proposal for every blocker
acceptance: Remote launcher runs on a server/control node, not local Mac.
At least one real child task is submitted through Control Plane to another node, or a hard Control Plane blocker is reported.
Fresh nodes receive capacity/readiness probes or explicit blocker classifications.
Agents are allowed to create follow-up repair tasks through Control Plane with idempotency keys and rate limits.
Per-node MIMO/subagent target up to 20 is capacity-gated and not assumed.
Global logical-agent target up to 1000 is represented as scheduler capacity, not uncontrolled OS processes.
No destructive commands, credential changes, firewall/VPN changes or production restarts occur.
Final result includes child task ids, lease owners, statuses, artifact paths, blockers and next dispatch wave.
